---
title: Test your agent
type: tutorial
audience: end-user
tier: standard
---

Now that you have an agent working, you need to write tests to ensure
that the quality of your answers doesn't degrade as you add context or
change the system instructions.

Tests live in a `.test.yml` file next to the agent. Name it after the agent —
`sleep.agentic.test.yml` tests `sleep.agentic.yml` — and list the questions
you care about along with the answer you expect:

```yaml sleep.agentic.test.yml
settings:
  runs: 5

cases:
  - prompt: "How many nights did I get high quality sleep?"
    expected: "23 nights"
  - prompt: "How many hours do I sleep on average?"
    expected: "About 7.2 hours per night"
    tags: [critical]
  - prompt: "What day do I typically get the most sleep?"
    expected: "Sunday"
```

You can add as many cases as you like. Each case runs `runs` times, and an LLM
judge checks whether each answer is factually consistent with `expected`.

<Note>
Only `.agentic.yml` agents can be tested, and only from `.test.yml` files.
Inline `tests:` blocks in `.agent.yml` or `.workflow.yml` files are no longer
supported.
</Note>

## Run your tests

Open the **Tests** page in the Oxygen IDE to see every test file in the
project, run them, and review past runs. Oxygen executes each case the
configured number of times and reports the results for each case.

To run the same tests from a terminal or CI, use the CLI:

```bash
# Every .test.yml file in the project
oxy test

# Just this agent's tests
oxy test sleep.agentic.test.yml
```

## What the judge ignores

Oxygen is built for data analysis, so the judge focuses on factual
correctness and ignores differences that don't change the answer:

- **Rounding and precision** — `$1,081,396` vs `$1,081,395.67`
- **Wording** — "Sales fell by 10%" vs "Sales decreased by 10%"
- **Formatting** — date formats, number formatting, whitespace

A run fails when its answer materially disagrees with `expected` — a different
number, the opposite trend, or a different conclusion.

## Quality gates in CI

Fail the build when accuracy drops below a threshold:

```bash
oxy test --min-accuracy 0.8
```

The command exits with code 1 if the score is below the threshold. Add
`--format json` for machine-readable output, or `--tag critical` to gate on a
subset of cases.

For every field and flag, see the [Testing reference](/guide/build/test-evaluate/testing).

At this point, you have a working agent as well as the ability to modify and
test this agent. Congratulations!
